idiom_name: OwnedHeaders insert with a serialized hop list (rust-rdkafka)
implementation_notes: rust-rdkafka models Kafka headers as a consuming builder - OwnedHeaders::new().insert(Header{ key, value: Option<&[u8]> }) passed to BaseRecord::set_headers - so appending a hop means rebuilding the header set: decode the incoming list, push the entry, re-encode and hand the new OwnedHeaders to the record. The mutable container of the classic structure is replaced by ownership-driven copies plus a serde-defined Hop struct; because values are bytes, the entry encoding is an explicit contract, and because insert consumes, branching requires cloning the headers per downstream record.
pitfalls: OwnedHeaders::insert consumes self, so 'append' is really 'rebuild' - clone the headers for each downstream record or a fan-out loses the trail.
Header.value is Option<&[u8]>: a header with a None value is legal, so an absent history and an empty history are indistinguishable unless you define the convention.
serde_json::from_slice on partner data must not unwrap(): a malformed history should drop the trail, not panic the consumer thread.
